title: Try, Record And Refine
objective: Practise your chosen arts skill, preserve the changing work and use the evidence to refine your next step.

blocks.text: GROW · Art · Trinity Arts Award Silver. Try, Record And Refine.
Objective: Practise your chosen arts skill, preserve the changing work and use the evidence to refine your next step.
Success evidence: Real arts practice, an ongoing record that retains earlier states, a reasoned adjustment and an exact location for the process evidence.
Use your own artwork, interests and practical choices. You can choose an abstract subject; you do not need to disclose private experiences.
40 minutes. Keep original work before making changes. Ask staff about safe tools and access.

This deck directly serves Silver Unit 1, Part 1B, Implement and review the arts challenge. Silver has TWO units, evidenced separately. This lesson belongs to Unit 1, Arts practice and pathways; keep its evidence labelled by unit and part. ONE Attempted allowed PER UNIT. Any Not Attempted = Below Pass. The whole Silver portfolio has a 20-file cap, not twenty per unit or one new file per lesson. The four assessment areas are art form knowledge and understanding, creativity, planning and review, and communication. Results are Pass or Below Pass only. Only an adviser trained at Silver may assess; delivery is through a validated centre. Staff must confirm those conditions; neither is asserted as completed here. The arts challenge must not focus on leadership. Advisers must not write pupil plans, reviews or evidence. Prompt, read or scribe the pupil’s exact words and check them back unchanged. Core, Extend and Challenge vary support within Silver, retaining the same evidence expectation and the pupil’s own choices. Digital evidence is organised by unit and part, with every locator naming the actual filename plus page, slide or timecode. A portfolio structure is an option, not an extra award rule. Samples, trial counts and prompts here are teaching scaffolds, not qualification quotas. Use accessible tools and communication without forced personal disclosure, compulsory filming or public posting. This forty-minute lesson supports a longer programme of real guided and independent practice; it does not claim all award hours are complete. Source: tools/artsaward/SPEC.json, Silver and universal rules. Part 1B requires ongoing evidence, someone ELSE’s review of the challenge and the pupil’s own final review. This deck begins sustained practice and process capture; an informal outside observation here does not replace the later required review of the challenge. The later 1B deck gathers that review and the pupil’s own final review. Work from the pupil’s actual 1A plan, teach a relevant technique before practice and preserve states before revision. The hatching demonstration is one option; adapt the taught method to the pupil’s chosen art process. Programme practice must continue for the real time their plan needs. Do not manufacture a completed challenge from one short lesson or reconstruct a lost baseline as though it were original.

stages.title: Arrival · retrieve
stages.data-ta1: Retrieve the actual plan and original work. Help preserve a usable before-state and prepare the relevant safe technique, rather than reconstructing earlier evidence.

blocks.text: Use the plan to begin real practice
Open your action plan and find the next practical step. Place the starting work beside it.
Read the purpose of that step. What artistic effect or skill are you trying to develop?
Check the resources and support before beginning. If something is missing, choose a safe alternative with staff or adjust the order honestly.
Keep a record of the work as it stands now. You may retain the original sample, make an agreed image or record a short description that identifies the detail.
Do this before changing the work. A note saying it used to look different cannot show the earlier state by itself.
Today begins a process record that will continue as your challenge develops.

stages.title: Starter · create the need
stages.data-ta1: Explain deliberate comparison without turning a controlled trial into an award quota or a universal rule for creative practice.

blocks.text: A change should teach you something
Artists often try, look and adjust. The useful part is noticing what a change does to the work.
You could alter the tool, pressure, paper and spacing together. The result may be interesting. It is then harder to tell which choice caused an effect.
To test one choice, keep other features steady. Try it on a small sample first. Then you can compare more clearly.
This is a practical method, not a rule that all art must be made one way. Your intention decides what is worth checking.
Choose a detail where a careful trial could help you understand your next step.

stages.title: I Do · model
stages.data-ta1: Demonstrate hatching and cross-hatching live. For a paper-form route, demonstrate an appropriate folded tab or support with actual materials before independent work.

blocks.text: Adult model: build tone with hatching
Watch the adult draw a small patch of parallel pencil lines. Hatching means building tone with rows of lines.
They keep a light grip and pull the strokes in the same direction. The spaces let some paper remain visible.
Next they make a fresh patch with closer spacing, while keeping similar pressure. They compare the tone. The first patch stays beside the new one.
They try another option on a fresh patch. They add light lines at a different angle. This is cross-hatching. The lines overlap and make a darker tone.
The adult looks for an effect that fits their example. They want a darker area that still shows the line texture. Pressing as hard as possible is not the only way to make it darker.
They choose a patch to develop and record what changed. The first samples stay visible so the comparison remains real.
If your challenge involves paper form, use the same thinking with the relevant making skill. Compare a folded tab or support before attaching it to the main piece.
Choose a deliberate action, examine its effect and decide what to keep. Your process does not have to match the adult's art or preference.

blocks.title: Keep the process visible
blocks.caption: Preserve, practise, compare and refine.
blocks.alt: Four boxes show keeping an earlier state before practice, comparing the result of a deliberate change and choosing the next step.

stages.title: We Do · everyone commits
stages.data-ta1: A is the clearer spacing comparison; B changes several features. C preserves evidence; D loses the earlier state. Discuss usefulness for the stated question rather than calling one artwork bad.

blocks.text: Visible trials: which answers the question?
Choose a card and keep your first answer ready. Point, write or hold its letter. Reveal your choice together, then explain your reason before hearing the adult’s model.
The adult wants to find what closer line spacing does. Compare these trial cards.
Which trial makes that question easier to answer? Explain what stayed steady and what changed.
The other trial may still produce useful art. It simply cannot tell us that spacing alone caused the difference.
Use this distinction when choosing what to test in your own work.

items: A · Same pencil, paper and light pressure; only the line spacing changes.
B · New paper, a darker pencil, harder pressure and closer line spacing.
C · Keep both trial patches and note the change beside them.
D · Rub out the first patch before there is a record, then write “better now”.

stages.title: I Do 2 · connect
stages.data-ta1: Support proportionate capture and actual dates. Keep outside observations accurately attributed; no invented quotations or signatures. Explain the distinction from the two required later reviews.

blocks.text: Keep evidence while the work changes
Your process record should show real actions, choices and changes. It is not a polished story written from memory at the end.
Keep the states that help explain a decision. A sample, a labelled photo or a short clip can be useful when it shows the relevant detail.
Name the actual action and date. Add what you noticed, then say why you chose the next step.
A ring around an area after it was changed does not preserve what was there before. Save the earlier state first.
Keep another person's words separate from your own thinking. If someone comments, record their actual words. Note who spoke or what role they had.
That comment may help you refine a step. It may concern one small detail. It is not a full review of the challenge.
Later, someone else will review the challenge and you will make your own final review. Today's ongoing record will help both reviewers see what really happened.

boxes.head: PROCESS RECORD
boxes.line1: what I did, noticed and changed

blocks.title: Practice evidence supports later reviews
blocks.caption: An ongoing record is not a substitute for the reviews.
blocks.alt: One panel shows process evidence and preserved states; the other shows the distinct later outside review and pupil final review.

stages.title: We Do 2 · lab
stages.data-ta1: Observe actual practice and help with access. Offer a relevant observation rather than an adult decision; preserve the pupil’s choice about the adjustment.

blocks.text: Practise and inspect the result
Begin the step you selected from your own plan. Use the technique staff have demonstrated for your materials.
For hatching, compare line spacing or direction without losing the earlier patch. For a folded tab, crease the joining edge clearly. Test the fit on scrap before fixing it in place.

For a tab join, fold the joining strip so it lies flat against the second piece. Align the edges before using the agreed adhesive. Support the join while it sets. Test the scrap gently and look for twisting or a gap before deciding to use it on the main form.
Pause where the result can tell you something. Look from the relevant angle or distance rather than inspecting only the easiest part.
Ask a partner or staff member what they notice. Focus their attention on the detail you are checking. Point to the work so the question is clear.
Record the response accurately if one is given. You decide whether and how it should affect your next action.

stages.title: Independent · evidence
stages.data-ta1: All tiers retain real practice, preserved changing states and the pupil’s reasoned decisions. Help capture evidence without replacing the pupil’s explanation.

blocks.text: Refine the work and keep the reason
Use what you noticed to choose a next step. You may repeat the method, adjust one feature or try a different safe approach.
Keep the earlier state before acting. Then practise the change and inspect its effect against your own intention.
Record what you did and why. Use a short note or spoken account of the detail. Simply saying the result is better does not explain the change.
Keep any outside observation clearly attributed. Add your own response rather than presenting the other person's view as yours.
Update the next step on your plan if needed. Continue the real practice for the time the challenge requires.
Save the evidence in Unit 1, Part 1B with the filename and page, slide or timecode.

items: Core · use your own plan. Practise the chosen skill with support. Preserve the starting work and useful changing states. Show what you changed and why. Keep an actual outside observation if received, with the practice record and exact location.

Extend · undertake the same real practice and keep an ongoing record in your own format. Compare a change with an earlier state. Explain your next decision. Distinguish an informal comment from the later review of the whole challenge.

Challenge · keep the same practice and process evidence. Test another feasible change that responds to a real difficulty, then explain which approach better serves your artistic intention. Keep evidence for that judgement.

stages.title: Exit · Audience and Influence
stages.data-ta1: Check actual evidence and next practice arrangements. Keep 1B marked as ongoing until its practice and both required reviews are genuinely available.

blocks.text: Leave a useful starting point for next time
Find the record of today's change. Can another person see what happened and why you chose it?
Check that the earlier state is still available. Repair a location note if it points at the wrong image or page.
Name the next practical step and anything that needs arranging. Keep practising between review points in the agreed programme time.
The process is still developing. A short comment today does not replace the outside review and your own final review of the challenge.

checks: The record shows real practice of my chosen arts challenge.
Earlier states were preserved before revision.
My change and reason are supported by actual work.
Outside comments are attributed and remain distinct from the required later reviews.
